title: Agents' listener tests no longer wait on or race each other
goal: CEO direction 2026-11-12 ("fix the port collisions between agents"). Several agents run their gates on one laptop at once. tests/common/mod.rs SocketTestGuard took ONE machine-wide lock with a blocking lock() and no time limit, so while any agent's host_only_privacy or peer_channel_hub test ran, or hung, every other agent's waited (board item 193: two test binaries asleep for over two minutes). The lock was keyed on the temp folder, so agents with a different TMPDIR did not share it at all, and host_only_privacy::free_wide_offset always scanned from offset 4000, so two unsynchronised runs chose the same block. Fix: common::reserve_port_block reserves a port block machine-wide (one lock file per block under a fixed folder, non-blocking try_lock, held until the test process exits, dropped by the OS on a crash), and both listener tests take their blocks through it; SocketTestGuard now serialises the listener tests within one checkout (lock keyed on the checkout path) instead of across the machine. No network or privacy assertion is changed.
limitations: Agents still share the laptop's CPU: a loaded machine can slow a listener test, which this does not address.
port_fallback deliberately starts an unpinned daemon and relies on the product's own next-free-block fallback; it takes no reservation.
A test that picks ports without reserve_port_block is not protected.
Linux x86_64 only; on Windows the lock folder is the per-user temp folder.
